newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Azeris, Russia's LUKoil sign $2 billion oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Azeris, Russia's LUKoil sign $2 billion oil deal.

text.p: Azerbaijan and LUKoil, Russia's biggest oil company, signed a $2 billion deal to explore and develop the D-222 block, known as the Yalama field, in the Azeri sector of the Caspian Sea, LUKoil said on Friday.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Azeri President Haydar Aliyev attended the signing ceremony of the widely anticipated deal on Thursday. Aliyev is on his first state visit to Russia to discuss issues ranging from oil to Armenia.

"On Thursday an agreement between oil company LUKoil and the Azeri state oil company SOCAR was signed in Moscow for the assessment, development and production sharing at the Azerbaijan block D222 in the Caspian Sea," LUKoil said in a statement.
Early estimates point to oil reserves of 50 million tonnes. LUKoil would have a 60 percent share in the venture, and SOCAR 40 percent.
"Proposed investment (in the project) is around $2 billion," said Pyotr Neyev, press spokesman for LUKoil. "This will be shared on the basis of 60 percent for LUKoil and 40 percent for SOCAR."

Oil produced from the field would be transported along an existing pipeline running from the Azeri capital Baku to Russia's Black Sea export outlet of Novorossiisk. It passes through Grozny and Tikhoretsk.
"The profitability of the plan for Russia increases significantly, given that the oil will pass through its territory," LUKoil said.

Moscow, Grozny and Baku are in intense negotiations over plans to use the same pipeline to carry early oil from the separate AIOC multi-billion-dollar international consortium working in the Azeri section of the Caspian.
AIOC, or Azerbaijan International Operating Company, led by British Petroleum Co Plc and Norway's Statoil, is due to start producing oil in August and is looking for a swift solution to the problem.
Azerbaijan's Aliyev on Friday held talks with Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov on the question of transporting early AIOC oil along the pipeline.
LUKoil president Vagit Alekperov said in the company statement that LUKoil hoped to strike more oil deals with Azerbaijan.
LUKoil already has stakes in three other joint projects with SOCAR to develop Caspian fields, and is negotiating joint development of the 200-million-tonne Inam field.
